lines.trans: Oh, the collectors' victim! Did you want something?
Yes. I came to say thank you and ask forgiveness.
What for?
I offended you. I was wrong.
That's how naughty you are.
Really, thank you.
But I just don't know how to thank you.
Alright, all sorts of things happen. Oh, come on.

But you don't know how! And I know!
You have lost your mind!

meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

бывать.gloss: to happen, to be (sometimes); to visit

meanings.en: to happen, to exist, there can be
meanings.note: 3rd person бывает = there is / can be
Часто бывать где-то. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to happen, to be (sometimes); to visit', paired with 'быть'.

examples.text: У мужчины бывает не только жена.
examples.trans: A man can have more than just a wife.

examples.text: У мужчины, мальчик, бывает не только жена. Это моя девушка.
examples.trans: A man, my boy, can have more than just a wife. She's my girlfriend.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Confirmation tag. Core Russian part meaning 'right, true, faithfully' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian part meaning 'right, true, faithfully' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: A man must help a woman, right?

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town.

meanings.note: Pointing at something. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.
Emphasis. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

всякий.gloss: every kind of, all sorts of, any

meanings.en: all sorts of, every kind of
meanings.note: всякое бывает = all sorts of things happen
На всякий случай = just in case. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'який').

examples.trans: Alright, all sorts of things happen.
Take an umbrella just in case.

examples.text: Ладно, всякое бывает. Ну что вы?
examples.trans: Alright, all sorts of things happen. Oh, come on.

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
At the start of a sentence. Core Russian pron meaning 'everything, all; that's it' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.
+ infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must, should; owe').

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'woman' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Твоя жена очень мудрая женщина. Ты её слушай.
examples.trans: Your wife is a very wise woman. You listen to her.

meanings.note: person harmed by a crime or accident
Приносить в жертву. Common feminine noun meaning 'victim; sacrifice' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: She became a victim of fraud.

examples.text: О, жертва коллекторов! Вы что-то хотели?

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
+ instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.

The thing that ends is the subject. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'кончиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to end, to be over', paired with 'заканчиваться'.
деньги закончились = the money ran out

examples.text: Всё, выборы закончились. Тебя начальник ждёт.
examples.trans: That's it, the election is over. Your boss is waiting for you.

meanings.note: A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Person who collects unpaid loans. Borrowed from Latin agent/instrument noun in '-tor' ('коллектор'). Common masculine noun meaning 'debt collector' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Agreeing, often reluctantly. Core Russian part meaning 'all right, OK' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: adult male; declines like a feminine -а noun

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
short forms: неправ, неправа, неправы

examples.trans: You are wrong in this argument.

examples.text: Был неправ. Простите. Я хочу закончить начатое.
examples.trans: I was wrong. Forgive me. I want to finish what I started.

meanings.note: Softer or playful for плохой. Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'хороший'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('bad, not good, naughty').

examples.trans: He is not a good person.

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: to offend, to hurt someone's feelings
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'идеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to offend, to hurt', paired with 'обижать'.

examples.trans: Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you.

examples.text: Извини, я не хотела обидеть. А ты что здесь делаешь?

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: всё уже позади = it's all behind us now

examples.trans: Calm down. Everything is behind us now.

examples.trans: Right, the operation goes on. Mikhail Mikhailovich, give Lavrov your help.

meanings.note: + dative. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помогать'.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'просить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to ask (for), to request', paired with 'просить'.

as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

meanings.note: On foot, once. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come, to arrive', paired with 'приходить'.

meanings.en: to sit down, to have a seat
meanings.note: Polite invitation: Присядьте!. Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'сесть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sit down (for a moment), to take a seat', paired with 'присаживаться'.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ойти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get off; (с ума) to go mad', paired with 'сходить'.
